summary.text: A 56-year-old man with severe paranoid schizophrenia and comorbid alcohol and cannabis abuse grew up under socio-economically beneficial conditions, raised fire at age nine, and left an apprenticeship in his early twenties with prodromal symptoms. A few years later he was admitted to a psychiatric unit with depressive symptoms and anxiety days before the index offense in the late 1980s; a Swiss court sentenced him to 8 years of imprisonment for a deliberate killing.

A first forensic expert evaluation in 1989 found impaired legal culpability due to a schizophrenic episode and recommended immediate in-patient treatment; at the time of the trial he showed formal thought disorders, and early signs of negative symptoms were described. He was malcompliant, irregularly refused psychopharmacological treatment and tried to escape multiple times; initial treatment attempts had no significant effect and an indefinite incarceration was executed in 1990.

Around 1995 the illness became chronified: positive symptoms and malcompliance were no longer observed and negative symptoms with drug-induced parkinsonism dominated, with impaired expressiveness, reduced speech and reduced psychosocial functioning. Long-term conventional antipsychotics had side effects, and psychotherapeutic and psychosocial approaches showed only limited success.

After more than 15 years of indefinite incarceration the sanction was converted in the late 2000s into an in-patient therapeutic measure under article 59; he was ordered another 8 years of sanction and eventually received conditional release with a 5-year probationary period until 2020. After almost 30 years in prisons and psychiatric institutions, with no relevant social contacts, he died in 2018 at age 56 from the consequences of a severe physical condition.
